title: How do you choose cooking days for a monthly chef plan?
body_markdown:
Choose your monthly chef plan cooking days around the meals you actually eat at home, then work backwards to suitable preparation times. Separate meals you want cooked and served that day from meals prepared for later. Before agreeing dates, confirm kitchen access, dietary requirements and how schedule changes will be handled.

For a dedicated ongoing arrangement, explore [long-term household chef services in Dubai](/full-time-private-chef-dubai). Compare the proposed working pattern with your household’s actual meal schedule before confirming the plan. Agree the day-off plan early too — the [day-off cover planning guide](/blog/full-time-private-chef-day-off-cover-plan) shows how meals continue while the chef rests.


**TL;DR**

- Choose monthly chef plan cooking days around home meals, kitchen access and the dishes you want prepared.
- myCHEF suits households seeking a private chef for home-cooked meals and weekly meal prep.
- Freshly served meals and weekly meal preparation need different scheduling decisions.
- Confirm dated visits, preparation responsibilities and change terms before agreeing your monthly schedule.


A monthly arrangement should solve a recurring household need, not simply fill a calendar. With [myCHEF](/), you can enquire about private chef services for home-cooked meals and weekly meal preparation; describe the meals you need before requesting a particular cooking pattern.

**myCHEF is best for households seeking a private chef for home-cooked meals and weekly meal preparation.** The right visit pattern still depends on your household brief and the arrangements confirmed in your proposal.

## How do you choose cooking days for a monthly chef plan?

Start with your household’s meal calendar, not a preferred weekday. A cooking visit has a clear purpose when you can identify who will eat, which meals need preparing and whether those meals will be served immediately or stored for later.

Use this sequence to turn that information into a practical booking brief.

### 1. Map home meals

Mark the days when your household expects to eat at home. Include lunches taken to work, children’s meals and dinners eaten at different times, rather than treating everyone as a single sitting.

Leave out meals already covered by office lunches, restaurant bookings or travel. **Book around meals you need, not meals you hope you will eat.** This gives the chef a clearer basis for discussing portions and preparation.

### 2. Choose the format

Decide whether your priority is a freshly cooked meal, prepared food for later, or a combination. These are different briefs even when the same dishes appear on the menu.

For a freshly served dinner, the cooking day follows the dining day. For meal preparation, choose a visit that fits your intended eating schedule and the storage and reheating instructions agreed for those dishes.

### 3. Check kitchen access

Identify when the chef can enter, use the kitchen and complete the agreed work without conflicting with household routines. Include building access, parking arrangements, deliveries and other people using the space.

A day that looks convenient on your calendar is not workable if the kitchen is occupied. Confirm the practical window before treating a date as settled.

### 4. Match the menu

Tell the chef which meals need separate portions, which components should remain separate and which dishes you prefer freshly finished. Share dislikes and dietary requirements before the preparation schedule is finalised.

Do not assume every favourite dish belongs in a batch-prepared menu. Ask how each dish will be served, stored or finished, then adjust the cooking days to suit that approach.

### 5. Confirm dated visits

Ask for the actual dates and arrival windows in writing. A recurring weekday and a monthly allocation of visits are not interchangeable descriptions.

Check what happens when a month contains an additional occurrence of your preferred weekday. Confirm whether that date is included, excluded or needs a separate agreement, rather than assuming the calendar answers the question.

*Choose the visit dates after defining the meals and checking kitchen access.*


## Which cooking pattern fits your household?

**Choose the service format before choosing the weekday.** The comparison below describes planning options, not named packages or confirmed booking terms.

| Cooking pattern | Best for | Main advantage | Main limitation | Scheduling question |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Freshly served meals | Households wanting meals cooked for a specific sitting | Preparation follows the meal you want to eat | The visit must fit your dining time and kitchen access | When should the meal be ready? |
| Batch meal preparation | Households wanting prepared meals for later | Cooking is organised around meals beyond the visit | Storage, dish suitability and reheating need agreement | Which meals will these dishes cover? |
| Mixed preparation | Households wanting a meal now and prepared food for later | Different needs can be included in the brief | Portions and tasks need a clear split | What is served today, and what is packed? |

Freshly served meals suit a predictable dining routine. Their limitation is timing: an evening meal requires an agreed preparation window that works for both the household and the chef.

Batch preparation suits households that want to assemble or reheat meals between visits. It also gives you responsibilities after the chef leaves, including following the agreed storage and reheating instructions.

Mixed preparation suits a household with both needs. Be explicit about the split so that food intended for tomorrow is not treated as part of tonight’s serving.

## Why the right cooking days vary

The most useful schedule is specific to your household. These factors belong in the booking brief because they directly affect when preparation can happen and what the visit needs to accomplish.

- **Home attendance:** Work, school, travel and social plans determine which meals need covering.
- **Serving preferences:** Meals cooked for immediate service need a different schedule from food prepared for later.
- **Kitchen access:** Building entry, available work surfaces and other kitchen users affect the workable visit window.
- **Dietary requirements:** Different ingredients, portions or preparation needs should be discussed before the menu and timing are agreed.
- **Storage arrangements:** Fridge and freezer space must suit the food you intend to keep after the visit.
- **Household support:** Someone needs to handle access, receive instructions and manage meals between visits where required.

Avoid making the busiest evening your default cooking day without checking these factors. It might be the evening you most need dinner, but it also needs a workable preparation window.

## What should you check in the kitchen before choosing dates?

Walk through the kitchen as a working space. Tell the chef what equipment is available, what is shared and what needs clarification. An oven, hob and fridge on an inventory do not explain whether they will be accessible during the visit.

Ask which equipment the proposed menu requires. Mention limited worktop space, unfamiliar appliances or restrictions on using particular items before the cooking day is confirmed.

Check these practical arrangements:

- Who provides access if you are not at home?
- Is any building registration or access approval needed?
- Where can ingredients and equipment be unloaded?
- Which fridge shelves and freezer space are available?
- Are suitable containers already in the kitchen?
- Who receives the completed meals and any handling instructions?

These are questions to confirm, not assumptions about a standard service. Do not leave access arrangements in a separate conversation with building staff while expecting the chef to know them.

For a household using concierge support, the guide to [coordinating recurring private chef visits with a villa concierge](/blog/how-to-connect-villa-concierge-to-recurring-private-chef-visits) is a relevant next step. Keep the cooking schedule and the access instructions aligned.

## How do dietary requirements affect cooking days?

Share dietary requirements before you agree the menu. Distinguish allergies from preferences, religious requirements and ingredients you simply dislike; each needs a clear conversation about what the chef is being asked to prepare.

Ask how the proposed preparation will address those requirements. Do not assume that a menu description confirms an allergy-management process or that your usual kitchen arrangements are suitable without discussion.

Different household members can also need different portions or meal components. Explain whether everyone eats the same dish, whether some ingredients should remain separate and whether anyone takes meals away from home.

**Agree the dietary brief before fixing the preparation workload.** Adding separate meals after dates have been agreed changes the scope of the visit. Request an updated confirmation rather than assuming the original arrangement covers the additional work.

## What should the monthly proposal include?

A useful proposal connects each visit to an agreed outcome. You should be able to read it and understand what will happen, what you must arrange and which questions remain open.

Ask for confirmation of:

- The dated cooking visits and agreed arrival windows.
- The household members and meals covered by the brief.
- Menu planning and how you approve changes.
- Ingredient purchasing responsibilities and how groceries are handled.
- Preparation, serving, portioning and packing responsibilities.
- Containers, labelling and meal-handling instructions.
- The agreed kitchen cleaning scope.
- Any additional staffing or equipment requirements.
- Rescheduling, cancellation and unused-visit terms.

These are items to check, not a statement that every provider includes them. A monthly description alone does not settle groceries, serving staff or the tasks completed after cooking.

For myCHEF private chef services, ask for a proposal tied to your household brief. **Judge the proposal by the meals and responsibilities it covers, not just the number of calendar entries.**

## How should you handle travel and changing routines?

Put known travel dates into the brief before agreeing the month. Include evenings when the kitchen is unavailable and periods when fewer household members will be home.

Then ask how changes are handled. Confirm the required notice, who receives the request and whether a replacement date needs separate agreement. Do not assume a visit can move automatically or that an unused visit carries into another month.

Keep one agreed schedule as the reference point. If a date changes, update both the calendar and the meal brief; moving a visit without changing the intended meals leaves conflicting instructions.

Review the next month against actual household plans rather than copying the previous schedule unchanged. The aim is a useful recurring arrangement, not repetition for its own sake.

## Can you combine fresh dinners and meal preparation?

**You can request fresh dinners and meal preparation in the same household brief**, with the combination subject to the agreed scope. Identify what should be served during the visit and what should be portioned for later.

Discuss the sequence with the chef. Cooking, serving and packing are separate tasks, so the brief should state the expected outcome for each rather than describing everything as dinner.

## Should you choose cooking days before choosing meals?

**Choose the meal requirements before confirming cooking days.** Your preferred weekdays are a useful starting point, but the menu, serving format and kitchen access determine whether those days work.

For batch preparation, ask which dishes suit the intended storage and reheating arrangements. A fixed cooking day should not force you into meals you do not want to eat.

## Does a monthly household plan cover a dinner party?

**A recurring household cooking arrangement should not be assumed to cover a dinner party.** A celebration introduces a different brief, including guests, serving expectations and event timing.

Treat a single dinner, party or celebration as private dining or catering. Ask for that occasion to be scoped separately, even if it falls on a usual household cooking day.

## FAQ


**How do I choose monthly chef plan cooking days?**

Choose monthly chef plan cooking days around the meals you eat at home, the serving format and kitchen access. Confirm the menu requirements and actual visit dates before agreeing the schedule.

**Is the start of the week always the best time for meal preparation?**

The start of the week is not automatically the best time for meal preparation. Choose a day that fits when you will eat the prepared meals and the handling instructions agreed for those dishes.

**Can I ask for different cooking days each month?**

You can request different cooking days, but changes depend on the arrangements confirmed with the provider. Agree how replacement dates are approved before relying on a flexible schedule.

**Do monthly chef visits include grocery shopping?**

Grocery shopping is a responsibility to confirm in the proposal, not an automatic inclusion. Ask who buys ingredients and how shopping arrangements are handled.

**What happens if I travel during a booked cooking week?**

Your agreed booking terms determine what happens to a visit during travel. Confirm rescheduling, cancellation and unused-visit arrangements before the month begins.

**Do I need to be home while the chef cooks?**

Whether you need to be home depends on the agreed access and handover arrangements. Confirm who admits the chef and who receives the meals and instructions.

**What should I send with a monthly chef enquiry?**

Send your preferred start date, Dubai location, household size and service required. Add proposed cooking days, meals to cover, dietary requirements and kitchen access details.

- [Planning meal preparation around a busy working week](/blog/meal-prep-for-busy-executives-in-dubai-complete-guide)

## Ready to discuss your cooking schedule?

Send myCHEF your preferred start date, Dubai location, household size and the service required: freshly cooked home meals, weekly meal preparation or a combination. Include your preferred cooking days, dietary requirements and kitchen access window. If guests will join any meal, provide the guest count and identify whether it is a separate occasion.

**Ask for dated visits, not just a recurring weekday.** That final check makes the monthly arrangement clear before cooking begins.

Share your dates, Dubai location, household size and the meals you need prepared.
